name: Alpha/beta tubulin heterodimer -- colchicine site
organism: Bos taurus (tubulina) + Rattus norvegicus (stathmin RB3) -- co-cristal 1SA0

structure.assembly: alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimer (colchicine site). Model 1SA0 holds 2 heterodimers (A/B and C/D) plus stathmin RB3 (chain E)

geometric_validation.note: Centre = the NATIVE position of the colchicine analogue CN2 (DAMA-colchicine) in co-crystal 1SA0, taking the most buried copy (chain D, beta-tubulin). Receptor = the whole of 1SA0 (2 heterodimers + stathmin RB3; the stathmin sits far from the colchicine site, so a local box of ~24 A does not reach it). POSITIVE arm of the control: colchicine redocked here must reproduce the pose (low RMSD).

colchicina.notes: Colchicine site at the alpha/beta intradimer interface. Specificity control: colchicine HERE must bind (positive); actin-binding drugs HERE must not (negative).

notes: Experimental structure 1SA0 (Ravelli et al. 2004, Nature) -- tubulin + DAMA-colchicine + stathmin RB3. Chosen over taxol/1JFF because colchicine binds the ISOLATED dimer, not only the assembled microtubule, has clean affinity data, and is a rigid molecule -- all of which make it a better docking control. Receptor prep: keep both heterodimers and the cofactors (GTP/GDP/Mg); stathmin (chain E) may be stripped during refinement, since it is far from the site.
